title: Mobbin portfolio project presentation research
scope: 10 desktop website sections and 10 native mobile app reference screens; mobile website captures were not verified

queries.query: Portfolio selected projects section with large project images, project names and short descriptions
Mobile portfolio website selected work section with project images stacked vertically, titles and descriptions
Design studio portfolio selected work section showing project previews and case study links
basement.studio featured projects with large images and contextual project descriptions
Designer portfolio profile showing published creative projects with cover images and project names
Behance creative profile portfolio showing project cover images and titles
Upwork freelancer portfolio showing published projects with images and titles
Fiverr seller Portfolio tab showing completed project images and project details
Portfolio website selected projects with thumbnails and names

entries.label: D01
entries.observation: Large project images occupy the left region; descriptions and discipline labels sit beside them, with project names at the far edge.
entries.strength: Explains the contribution alongside the work.
entries.tradeoff: Wide separation can make image/text association harder; the copy is compact.
entries.application: Strong candidate for three projects: one substantial row per product, using supplied role and scope facts.

entries.label: D02
entries.observation: Unequal image sizes and vertical offsets form two columns. Each project has a name, short description and small category labels.
entries.strength: Adds visual rhythm while preserving context.
entries.tradeoff: Offsets complicate reading order; gaps lengthen the section.
entries.application: Explore the owner's Huncwot preference through an expressive grid with explicit document order.

entries.label: D03
entries.observation: A large Selected work heading leads into adjacent image columns; names and small labels sit over each tile's bottom.
entries.strength: Makes digital product visuals prominent.
entries.tradeoff: Dark overlays reduce detail; text needs careful contrast.
entries.application: Show real interface previews with project titles legible independently of the image.

entries.label: D04
entries.pattern: One dominant project and one smaller project
entries.observation: A larger portrait image sits beside a smaller image; project names and discipline labels appear below.
entries.strength: Creates deliberate emphasis.
entries.tradeoff: The smaller tile makes one project secondary; tiny captions explain little.
entries.application: Explore a lead project plus supporting projects after project priority is supplied.

entries.label: D05
entries.observation: Selected Projects sits above category pills and an even two-column image grid; titles and project-type descriptions sit below.
entries.strength: Supports comparison through a predictable structure.
entries.tradeoff: The atmospheric backdrop competes with information; filters add controls.
entries.application: Borrow image/name/description grouping. Three projects do not yet justify filters.

entries.label: D06
entries.observation: Each row includes a project name, short statement and metadata, followed by a horizontal strip of many project images.
entries.strength: Shows depth within each project.
entries.tradeoff: Tiny previews are hard to read for interface work; horizontal behavior is unverified.
entries.application: Useful for a sequence of product screens if a primary visual remains readable.

entries.label: D07
entries.observation: Three image columns share a top edge and carry centered names and short explanatory copy.
entries.strength: Fits a three-project selection compactly.
entries.tradeoff: Equal priority may not suit unequal projects; small UI previews hide detail.
entries.application: Direct comparison candidate for the three Moriz products, with clear descriptions.

entries.label: D08
entries.observation: Dark horizontal rows pair project names with discipline labels and client marks; one row includes a narrow visual strip.
entries.strength: Makes work information scannable.
entries.tradeoff: Most work is not visibly pictured; hover or expansion cannot be inferred.
entries.application: Possible future archive pattern; a visual homepage showcase exposes design quality more directly.

entries.label: D09
entries.observation: A Work heading and project count lead to a smaller left image and larger right image; both have names and explanatory captions.
entries.strength: Varies emphasis without separating context from imagery.
entries.tradeoff: The large archive differs from a three-project homepage.
entries.application: Borrow captions and intentional scale variation while keeping the selection small.

entries.label: D10
entries.pattern: Two featured projects and archive link
entries.observation: An oversized WORK heading leads to two large images with title/client captions; a See all projects link follows.
entries.strength: Separates selected work from an archive.
entries.tradeoff: Covers provide little product explanation; the archive link requires a real destination.
entries.application: Explore large visuals plus one sentence of product context. Add an archive action only if a Projects page is selected.

entries.label: M01
entries.observation: A compact creator bar and Work/About tabs precede a two-column grid of covers with title strips.
entries.strength: Lets work dominate with a small identity area.
entries.tradeoff: Narrow columns leave little space for context.
entries.application: Useful for a larger archive; compare with a single column for three products.

entries.label: M02
entries.observation: A cover, avatar, name, metrics and actions precede Work/About tabs and two-column project cards.
entries.strength: Connects the work to its author.
entries.tradeoff: The identity area delays projects; follower metrics are not product outcomes.
entries.application: Use a short section introduction instead of duplicating a large homepage identity block.

entries.label: M03
entries.observation: The profile is followed by a service preview, a Logo group heading and two-column named covers.
entries.strength: Shows a visible way to group related work.
entries.tradeoff: Services and completed work can blur together; grouping consumes space.
entries.application: Relevant if future portfolio breadth warrants groups. Three current products do not establish a taxonomy.

entries.label: M04
entries.observation: A Portfolio heading and Published/Drafts tabs precede two-column UI covers with multiline descriptive titles and pagination.
entries.strength: Titles explain more than client names alone.
entries.tradeoff: Small collages hide interface detail; owner controls do not belong in a public showcase.
entries.application: Borrow descriptive product titles and use a readable primary screen; omit editing controls.

entries.label: M05
entries.observation: A Portfolio tab is followed by explanatory copy, a share action and two-column project cards with titles and media counts.
entries.strength: Explains the purpose of the work and indicates more project material.
entries.tradeoff: Profile/navigation occupy space; truncated titles lose context.
entries.application: Use a concise introduction and clear case-study action with full project names.

entries.label: M06
entries.pattern: Small portfolio teaser with See All
entries.observation: My portfolio and See All frame a two-by-two collage; its final tile carries a +140 more overlay. Reviews follow.
entries.strength: Distinguishes a short teaser from a large archive.
entries.tradeoff: Images lack visible names; the quantity cue suits a large archive.
entries.application: Compare a compact teaser with a complete three-project section. Keep names visible; do not invent counts.

entries.label: M07
entries.observation: Two uneven-height columns show project imagery, full titles and media counts under a compact portfolio header.
entries.strength: Accommodates varied image proportions.
entries.tradeoff: Uneven positions complicate scanning; some titles are long.
entries.application: Compare visual variety with an ordered single column for Hebrew product descriptions.

entries.label: M08
entries.observation: Below the creator identity, a Projects row shows one preview card and part of another, each with a title; interest chips follow.
entries.strength: The partial next card indicates more work.
entries.tradeoff: Later projects need sideways discovery; swipe behavior is untested.
entries.application: Possible secondary gallery. Keep primary projects reachable through vertical scrolling.

entries.label: M09
entries.observation: A video preview precedes a photographer's narrative paragraph and a two-column set of photographs.
entries.strength: Pairs explanation with multiple supporting images.
entries.tradeoff: This is an editorial photography story, not a project index; it takes more space.
entries.application: Useful for a featured product or future case study: overview followed by meaningful interface details.

entries.label: M10
entries.observation: A creator profile states an app count and shows a two-column grid of rounded cards, each with an image and short app name.
entries.strength: Keeps products visibly distinct and named.
entries.tradeoff: Icon-like images expose less interface detail; social actions are platform-specific.
entries.application: Adapt clear identification with real product screenshots rather than decorative icons.
